source.title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the numerical index n(ℓ_p) of the classical sequence space ℓ_p is strictly positive for every p ≠ 2.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Is n(ℓp) positive for every p 6= 2?

accepted.question_text: For the real two-dimensional space ℓ_p^2 with 1 < p < ∞, determine whether its numerical index equals sup_{t∈[0,1]} |t^{p-1} - t| / (1 + t^p).

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Is it true that, in the real case, n(ℓ2p) = sup t∈[0,1] |t^{p−1} − t| / (1 + t^p) for every 1 < p < ∞?

accepted.question_text: For the complex two-dimensional space ℓ_p^2 with 1 < p < ∞, determine whether its numerical index equals p^(-1/p) q^(-1/q), where 1/p + 1/q = 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Is it true that, in the complex case, n(ℓ2p) = 1 / p^(1/p) q^(1/q) for every 1 < p < ∞?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the numerical index of ℓ_p equals the numerical index of its two-dimensional version ℓ_p^2 for every 1 < p < ∞; that is, whether n(ℓ_p) = n(ℓ_p^2).

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Is it true that n(ℓp) = n(ℓ2p) for every 1 < p < ∞?

accepted.question_text: Compute the numerical index of real C*-algebras and of isometric preduals of real W*-algebras.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Compute the numerical index of real C∗-algebras and isometric preduals of real W∗-algebras.

accepted.question_text: Compute the numerical index of the following Banach spaces: C^m[0,1] with any of its usual norms, Lip(K) for a complete metric space K, Lorentz spaces, and Orlicz spaces.
accepted.context_brief: Classical spaces with unknown numerical index

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Compute the numerical index of C m[0, 1] ..., Lip(K) ..., Lorentz spaces, and Orlicz spaces.

accepted.question_text: Compute the numerical index for additional families of finite-dimensional Banach spaces, in particular for complex analogues of the polyhedral examples studied in the cited work [59].

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Compute the numerical index for other families of finite-dimensional Banach spaces. In particular, it would be interesting to get the complex analog of the results in [59].

accepted.question_text: Let Y be a dual Banach space. Determine whether there always exists a predual X of Y such that the numerical index of X equals the numerical index of Y.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Let Y be a dual space. Does there exist a predual X of Y such that n(X) = n(Y )?

accepted.question_text: If X is a Banach space with the Radon–Nikodým property, determine whether its numerical index always agrees with the numerical index of its dual; that is, whether n(X) = n(X*).

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Let X be a Banach space with the Radon-Nikodým property. Is it true that n(X) = n(X∗)?

accepted.question_text: Let Y be a dual Banach space that admits a unique predual X up to isometric isomorphism. Determine whether n(Y) must equal n(X).

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Let Y be a dual space admitting a unique predual X (up to isometric isomorphisms). Is it true that n(Y ) = n(X)?

accepted.question_text: Find necessary and sufficient conditions, stated without quantifying over operators, for a Banach space to have numerical index 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for a Banach space to have numerical index 1 which do not involve operators.

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a Banach space with numerical index 1. Must every extreme point x of the unit ball B_X and every extreme point x* of the dual unit ball B_{X*} satisfy |x*(x)| = 1?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Let X be a Banach space with numerical index 1. Is it true that |x∗(x)| = 1 for every x∗ ∈ ext(BX∗ ) and every x ∈ ext(BX )?

accepted.question_text: If X is a Banach space with numerical index 1, determine whether there must exist a norming subset A of the dual unit sphere S_{X*} such that |x**(a*)| = 1 for every extreme point x** of B_{X**} and every a* in A.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Let X be a Banach space with numerical index 1. Does there exist a norming subset A of SX∗ such that |x∗∗(a∗)| = 1 for every x∗∗ ∈ ext(BX∗∗ ) and every a∗ ∈ A?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a real almost-CL-space that is not a CL-space.

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Is there any real almost-CL-space which is not a CL-space?

accepted.question_text: If a Banach space X satisfies n(X) = 1, determine whether X must be lush.

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Let X be a Banach space with n(X) = 1. Is X lush?

accepted.question_text: Characterize those Banach spaces X for which there exists an equivalent norm on X having numerical index 1; equivalently, characterize when 1 belongs to the renorming set N(X).

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Characterize those Banach spaces which can be equivalently renormed to have numerical index 1.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists an infinite-dimensional complex reflexive Banach space that can be equivalently renormed to have numerical index 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Does there exist an infinite-dimensional complex reflexive space which can be renormed to have numerical index 1?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional real Banach space such that some equivalent norm on X has numerical index 1, that is, 1 ∈ N(X). Must the dual space X* contain an isomorphic copy of ℓ_1?
accepted.context_brief: Renorming and ℓ_1 in the dual

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Let X be an infinite-dimensional (real) Banach space satisfying that 1 ∈ N (X). Does X∗ contain ℓ1?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an infinite-dimensional real Banach space such that 1 ∈ N(X). Must X contain an isomorphic copy of c_0 or ℓ_1?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Let X be an infinite-dimensional (real) Banach space satisfying that 1 ∈ N (X). Does X contain c0 or ℓ1?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a Banach space X contains an infinite-dimensional subspace Y such that Y admits an equivalent norm with numerical index 1. Determine whether X must also admit an equivalent norm with numerical index 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Let X be a Banach space containing an infinite-dimensional subspace Y such that 1 ∈ N (Y ). Is it true that 1 ∈ N (X)?

accepted.question_text: If a Banach space X contains a subspace isomorphic to c_0, ℓ_1, C[0,1], or L_1[0,1], determine whether X must admit an equivalent norm with numerical index 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Let X be a Banach space containing a subspace isomorphic to either c0 , ℓ1, C[0, 1], or L1[0, 1]. Is it true that 1 ∈ N (X)?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space such that ℓ_1 embeds into X*. Determine whether X must admit an equivalent norm with numerical index 1, i.e. whether 1 ∈ N(X).

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Let X be a Banach space such that ℓ1 ⊆ X∗. Is it true that 1 ∈ N (X)?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary Banach space X, determine whether the supremum of the numerical indices of all equivalent norms on X is always 1; equivalently, whether sup N(X) = 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Is it true that sup N (X) = 1 for every Banach space X ?

accepted.question_text: Find characterizations, not phrased in terms of operators, of real Banach spaces whose numerical index is 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Find characterizations of Banach spaces with numerical index 0 which do not involve operators.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a real Banach space with a nonzero skew-hermitian operator. Determine whether X must contain a subspace that carries a complex structure.

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Let X be a real space which has a non-null skew-hermitian operator. Does X contain a subspace with a complex structure?

accepted.question_text: Describe the finite-dimensional real Banach spaces whose numerical index is 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Describe the finite-dimensional real Banach spaces with numerical index 0.

accepted.question_text: For each dimension n, determine which values can occur as the dimension of the Lie algebra Z(X) of skew-hermitian operators on an n-dimensional real Banach space X.

evidence.quote: Problem 27. Figure out what are the possible values for the dimension of Z(X) when dim(X) = n.

accepted.question_text: Determine the possible values of dim Z(X) when X is a 5-dimensional real Banach space.

evidence.quote: Problem 28. What are the possible values for the dimension of Z(X) when X is a 5-dimensional real Banach space?

accepted.question_text: Let M_m denote the class of m-dimensional real normed spaces with numerical index 1. Determine whether there exists a universal constant c > 0 such that every X in M_m satisfies d(X, ℓ_2^m) ≥ c √m in Banach–Mazur distance.

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Does there exists a universal constant c > 0 such that d(X, ℓm2 ) > c √m for every m > 1 and every X ∈ Mm?

accepted.question_text: For the set M_m of m-dimensional real normed spaces with numerical index 1, determine the diameter of M_m in Banach–Mazur distance and whether it is asymptotically close to the diameter of the full space N_m of all m-dimensional normed spaces.

evidence.quote: Problem 30. What is the diameter of Mm? Is it (asymptotically) close to the diameter of Nm?

accepted.question_text: For the Banach–Mazur metric on the class N_m of all m-dimensional real normed spaces, determine the largest possible distance from a point of N_m to the subset M_m of spaces with numerical index 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 31. What is the biggest possible distance from an element of Nm to the set Mm?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space with the alternative Daugavet property and assume X contains no copy of ℓ_1. Determine whether X must then satisfy n(X) = 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Let X be a Banach space which does not contain any copy of ℓ1 and having the alternative Daugavet property. Is it true that n(X) = 1?

accepted.question_text: If X has the alternative Daugavet property, determine whether every operator T in L(X) that fixes no copy of ℓ_1 must satisfy v(T) = ||T||.
accepted.context_brief: Operators fixing no copy of ℓ_1

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Let X be a Banach space with the alternative Daugavet property. Is it true that v(T ) = kT k for every operator T ∈ L(X) fixing no copy of ℓ1?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex Banach space such that its underlying real space X_R has the alternative Daugavet property. Determine whether X, equivalently X_R, must have the Daugavet property.

evidence.quote: Problem 34. Let X be a complex Banach space such that XR has the alternative Daugavet property. Does it follow that X (equivalently XR) has the Daugavet property?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a Banach space X for which the second-order polynomial numerical index strictly drops on passing to the bidual, that is, n^(2)(X**) < n^(2)(X).
accepted.context_brief: Bidual behavior of polynomial numerical index

evidence.quote: Problem 35. Is there a Banach space X such that n(2)(X∗∗) < n(2)(X)?

accepted.question_text: Compute the polynomial numerical indices of complex Hilbert spaces and of ℓ_1.
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial numerical indices of classical spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 36. Compute the polynomial numerical indices of complex Hilbert spaces and of ℓ1.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the second-order polynomial numerical index satisfies n^(2)(C[0,1]) = 1 in the real case, and whether n^(2)(L_1[0,1]) = 1 in the real case and/or in the complex case.
accepted.context_brief: Second-order polynomial numerical index for C[0,1] and L_1[0,1]

evidence.quote: Problem 37. Is n(2)(C[0, 1]) = 1 in the real case? Is n(2)(L1[0, 1]) = 1 in the real and/or in the complex case?

accepted.question_text: Let {X_λ} be a family of complex Banach spaces. Determine whether n^(k)([⊕_λ X_λ]_{c_0}) = n^(k)([⊕_λ X_λ]_{ℓ_∞}) = inf_λ n^(k)(X_λ).
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial numerical index of c_0 and ℓ_∞ sums

evidence.quote: Problem 38. Let {Xλ : λ ∈ Λ} be a family of complex Banach spaces. Is it true that n(k)([⊕λ∈ΛXλ]c0 ) = n(k)([⊕λ∈ΛXλ]ℓ∞ ) = infλ n(k)(Xλ) ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex Banach space. Determine whether the k-th polynomial numerical index of the vector-valued continuous-function space C(K,X) always equals n^(k)(X).

evidence.quote: Problem 39. Let X be a complex Banach space. Is n(k)(C(K, X)) equal to n(k)(X)?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space, let μ be a positive σ-finite measure, and let k > 2. Determine whether there is any general relationship between n^(k)(L_1(μ,X)) or n^(k)(L_∞(μ,X)) and n^(k)(X).
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial numerical index of Bochner spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 40. Let X be a Banach space, µ a positive σ-finite measure and k > 2. Is there any relationship between n(k)(L1(µ, X)) (resp. n(k)(L∞(µ, X))) and n(k)(X)?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed integer k > 2, describe the sets of all values attained by the k-th polynomial numerical index n^(k)(X) as X ranges over real Banach spaces and as X ranges over complex Banach spaces.

evidence.quote: Problem 41. For a given k > 2, describe the sets { n(k)(X) : X real Banach space } and { n(k)(X) : X complex Banach space }.

accepted.question_text: Study real Banach spaces X with second-order polynomial numerical index n^(2)(X) = 0. In particular, determine whether such spaces must also satisfy the ordinary numerical index condition n(X) = 0, and answer the same question in the finite-dimensional setting.

evidence.quote: Problem 42. Study the real Banach spaces X satisfying n(2)(X) = 0. For instance, do they satisfy that n(X) = 0? What is the answer for finite-dimensional spaces?

accepted.question_text: Characterize complex Banach spaces X for which n^(k)(X) = 1 for every k > 2. In particular, determine whether every infinite-dimensional such space must contain a copy of c_0.
accepted.context_brief: Complex spaces with maximal polynomial numerical indices

evidence.quote: Problem 43. Characterize the complex Banach spaces X satisfying n(k)(X) = 1 for all k > 2. In particular, do they always contain a copy of c0 in the infinite-dimensional case?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a real Banach space X other than the scalar field ℝ itself such that n^(2)(X) = 1.

evidence.quote: Problem 44. Is there any real Banach space X different from R such that n(2)(X) = 1?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a Banach space X for which the limit of the sequence of polynomial numerical indices lim_{k→∞} n^(k)(X) exists and is neither 0 nor 1.
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic behavior of polynomial numerical indices

evidence.quote: Problem 45. Is there any Banach space X for which lim k→∞ n(k)(X) 6= 0, 1?
